title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic bcc NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy prepared by arc melting/casting and homogenization (single-phase bcc, polycrystalline).
recollection.intervention: Guess: Partial substitution with rhenium (~5–10 at.%) to form NbMoTaWRe, followed by ion irradiation (e.g., in situ 1 MeV Kr2+ at ~673–773 K) to a few dpa; characterized by TEM (loop/void analysis), APT or diffuse scattering (for SRO), and nanoindentation.
recollection.structure: Guess: Both alloys remained single-phase bcc; the Re-containing alloy showed a markedly lower density and size of irradiation-induced dislocation loops and suppressed void/bubble formation relative to NbMoTaW at comparable dose and temperature.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Re addition induces chemical short-range order and strong solute–defect binding in the bcc matrix, increasing point-defect recombination and reducing defect mobility; enhanced lattice distortion and local energy landscape fluctuations act as effective defect traps, thereby suppressing loop growth and void swelling.
recollection.results: Guess: At ~3–5 dpa and ~773 K, the Re-added alloy exhibited ~50–70% lower dislocation loop density (e.g., from ~1–2×10^22 m^-3 down to ~3–7×10^21 m^-3), ~30–50% smaller mean loop diameters (e.g., ~8–10 nm down to ~4–6 nm), near-elimination or strong reduction of void swelling (e.g., from ~0.2–0.3% down to ≤0.05%), and ~30–50% lower irradiation-induced hardening (e.g., ΔH reduced from ~2 GPa to ~1 GPa) compared with NbMoTaW.

score.note: The recollection misidentifies the film synthesis, Re concentration, irradiation species, energy, temperature, and dose. It correctly suggests a BCC matrix and suppression of irradiation-induced bubbles/voids, but incorrectly emphasizes dislocation-loop statistics and omits the observed grain refinement, excess free volume, amorphous grain-boundary regions, and grain-boundary bubble segregation. The proposed lattice-distortion/defect-trapping and enhanced recombination mechanism is substantially consistent with the paper, although chemical short-range order and strong solute–defect binding were not the reported basis. All numerical results are invented and do not match the He-implantation conditions or measured mechanical results.
